topic: K1 identify the exact predictable AIPW quadratic-variation interval in growing block-adaptive complete randomization by block-weighted multi-marginal OT. K2 give sorting for two arms and a finite LP for fixed K. K3 prove plug-in endpoint consistency over adaptive histories. K4 prove completion-sharp conservative martingale Wald inference from the upper endpoint. Include the {-1,-1,1,1} coupling witness and Newby JAMA 2025 mental-health minitrials consumer; never condition on the final adaptive path. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Because next-block counts are prior-history predictable, centered block scores should be martingale differences, eliminating cross-block terms in predictable quadratic variation. Each remaining block variance is linear in an unidentified within-unit residual coupling with observed armwise marginals, hence a multi-marginal transport endpoint. Rearrangement handles two arms; a fixed-K empirical LP handles more. The witness yields contrast-square zero versus four, confirming nontrivial width. Nuisance estimation and history-uniform endpoint convergence remain unchecked. Stable residual empirical laws plausibly make empirical transport endpoints uniformly estimable. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove adaptive AIPW centering and uniform plug-in convergence without conditioning on realized final counts, then show the upper predictable-QV endpoint gives uniformly valid, completion-sharp self-normalized coverage. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate a two-block design whose second allocation depends on first-block outcomes and calculate every covariance. Stop if any unidentified cross-block term survives predictable conditioning or if blockwise OT fails to equal the feasible quadratic-variation range.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the predictable quadratic variation of a contrast AIPW martingale under growing block-adaptive complete randomization be sharply identified, using only prior histories and never the realized final adaptive path, as a block-weighted multi-marginal optimal-transport interval?

source_refs.claim: Develops finite-population design-based IPW/AIPW theory for adaptive and block-adaptive designs, but its improved covariance estimator is sharp only under additive residuals.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao

source_refs.claim: Characterizes exact causal partial-identified sets by K-marginal optimal transport and treats quadratic variance objectives for nonadaptive marginal laws.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian
source_refs.venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 258

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp variance bounds and consistent endpoint estimators for two-arm completely randomized experiments from the unidentified potential-outcome coupling.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.excerpt: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1.
Scoped out of v1: ... the fixed-treatment-count design class ... and a variance estimator / Wald inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two literatures stop on opposite sides of the junction. Li and Zhao provide the finite-population martingale and block-adaptive AIPW chassis but obtain covariance sharpness only under additive residuals; Gao, Ge, and Qian provide exact K-marginal transport sets for static marginals; and Aronow, Green, and Lee provide the two-arm static rearrangement case. The prior CausalSmith cross-world construction likewise reduces only one two-arm covariance to a scalar Fréchet interval, while the accepted ±1 design result explicitly excludes fixed-count designs and variance inference. The first proof obligation is a fully enumerated two-block conditional covariance calculation: pre-block-measurable counts and past-only nuisance fits must make centered block scores martingale differences, after which every remaining unidentified term must be representable by one within-block K-marginal residual coupling. Any unidentified cross-block term, or failure of summed block support functions to exhaust the globally feasible predictable-QV set, kills the proposed reduction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality theorem identifying the feasible predictable-QV set as the interval of block-weighted K-marginal OT extrema, with a two-arm quantile-sorting formula, an exact fixed-K empirical transportation LP with primal-dual attainment, and a {-1,-1,1,1} completion attaining contrast-square values zero and four.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from adaptive allocation to finite-population AIPW inference and then to the unresolved conservativeness of covariance estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive designs make assignments history-dependent -> finite-population potential outcomes require design-based martingale analysis -> adaptive AIPW covariance remains conservative outside residual additivity -> identify its exact coupling-compatible predictable-QV envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Represent missing cross-world dependence as a K-marginal Kantorovich problem and prove that extrema over couplings exhaust the identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each conditional block variance is a quadratic linear functional of an unobserved joint residual law whose armwise marginals are observed, exactly the object handled by their MOT argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Fréchet-Hoeffding rearrangement bounds, empirical quantiles, and endpoint consistency to construct asymptotically narrowest conservative Wald intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the two-arm static special case of the desired sharp variance endpoint and supplies both the sorting proof and its inference interpretation.

method_exemplars.technique: Express adaptive AIPW errors as martingale differences and prove block-adaptive finite-population limit and coverage results.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its filtration and block-score construction are the natural chassis on which the transport envelope must be installed.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what stability, overlap, block-growth, and predictable nuisance-learning conditions are empirical block-weighted multi-marginal transport endpoints uniformly consistent over all admissible adaptive histories without conditioning on realized final block counts?

source_refs.claim: Proves plug-in MOT convergence rates, including minimax-optimal rates for a quadratic variance cost, for fixed nonadaptive marginal distributions.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian
source_refs.venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 258

source_refs.claim: Uses optimal-transport duality and functional delta methods to obtain endpoint limit theory and bootstrap inference for functionals of a joint potential-outcome distribution.
source_refs.author: Daniel Ober-Reynolds

source_refs.claim: Allows nonexchangeable finite populations and adaptively constructed outcome regressions, but does not establish uniform convergence of sharp OT variance endpoints.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency
Define one law-independent sequential algorithm class as measurable assignment kernels q_t(a | x, h)

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing OT plug-in theory controls a functional of ordinary empirical marginals, and the prior cross-world proposal proves consistency only for independent unpaired pilots over a fixed compact basis class. Here the endpoint is a random weighted sum of blockwise OT values whose weights, arm counts, residual transformations, nuisance estimates, and effective sample sizes are predictable functions of earlier outcomes. The sequential-design reviewer also requires a single law-independent class of history-measurable assignment kernels before induced propensities are analyzed. The missing proof step is therefore a history-uniform empirical-process and OT-stability modulus for predictable triangular arrays; freezing final counts would erase precisely the adaptive paths over which the result must be uniform.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving uniform-in-history convergence in probability, in endpoint value and interval Hausdorff distance and preferably with a rate, of the empirical multi-marginal transport interval to the population predictable-QV interval under explicit overlap, residual-law stability, nuisance-remainder, and growing-block conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its nonexchangeable finite-population framing and past-only adaptive outcome models match the destination regime.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive block designs produce nonstationary finite populations -> AIPW permits past-only black-box adjustment -> sharp variance requires empirical residual marginals -> prove transport endpoints converge uniformly across adaptive histories

method_exemplars.technique: Control the plug-in multi-marginal OT value for quadratic costs and derive convergence and minimax rates from empirical marginal approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator is the same quadratic MOT value map, but evaluated blockwise on predictable, adaptively generated residual marginals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use OT duality, endpoint-map differentiability, and functional delta or bootstrap arguments to transfer marginal-law convergence into endpoint inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies limit-theory machinery for OT endpoints; the adaptive result must replace its first empirical-process step by a martingale approximation uniform over histories.

method_exemplars.technique: Control adaptive finite-population AIPW arrays with predictable nuisance estimates under explicit design regularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those bounds supply the adaptive-history control absent from static OT plug-in arguments.

open_problems.open_problem: Does Studentizing a block-adaptive AIPW estimator by the plug-in upper endpoint of its sharp predictable-QV interval yield uniformly valid and completion-sharp conservative martingale Wald inference without variance stabilization or conditioning on the final adaptive path?

source_refs.claim: Obtains fixed-horizon asymptotic normality for predictably scored AIPW/DML under adaptive assignment by Studentizing with realized quadratic variation when predictable quadratic variation remains random.
source_refs.author: Gabriel Saco

source_refs.claim: Shows for static complete randomization that the sharp upper variance bound yields the asymptotically narrowest conservative Wald interval.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.claim: Develops a sharp variance estimator and causal-bootstrap refinements for nonadaptive stratified randomized experiments.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Ke Zhu, and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: Establishes conservative design-based Wald coverage for adaptive AIPW estimators, with covariance sharpness only under a residual-additivity condition.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: same-path realized-QV sandwich is uniformly pivotal and asymptotically untruncated
not a pure fixed-finite-population randomization theorem.
a variance estimator / Wald inference for the chosen design.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available inferential results normalize by different objects. Saco uses observed realized quadratic variation in a sequential setting; Li and Zhao use a design-based conservative covariance estimator; and Aronow, Green, and Lee and Yu, Zhu, and Liu prove sharp upper-bound inference only for nonadaptive complete or stratified randomization. The prior adaptive-bandit proposal likewise supplies a same-path realized-QV pivot but explicitly disclaims a pure fixed-population theorem, while the accepted balanced-sign proposal leaves variance and Wald inference open. Replacing point studentization by a random estimated upper completion envelope needs uniform history-wise consistency plus a martingale limit theorem tolerant of a one-sided random scale. Completion sharpness additionally requires an attaining residual coupling and an admissible sequence on which the upper endpoint is the actual asymptotic QV; terminal-path Slutsky arguments cannot supply that unconditional adaptive statement.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A self-normalized martingale limit and uniform liminf-coverage theorem for the Wald interval scaled by the plug-in upper predictable-QV endpoint over all compatible completions and adaptive histories, together with an attaining completion showing that any asymptotically smaller endpoint-based scale fails somewhere in the compatibility class.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the fixed-horizon problem created by random predictable quadratic variation and motivates self-normalization without forcing variance stabilization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive propensities keep changing -> predictable variance need not approach a deterministic constant -> fixed-variance Wald inference can miscalibrate -> self-normalize using a sharp conservative predictable-QV envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Make past-only AIPW scores exact martingale differences and apply fixed-horizon self-normalized martingale limit theory without predictable-variance stabilization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same score martingale is required; the new proof must replace realized quadratic variation by a uniformly consistent conservative endpoint.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove upper-endpoint attainability over compatible potential-outcome couplings and translate it into asymptotic narrowness of conservative Wald intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its attainability argument is the static prototype for completion sharpness rather than mere conservative domination.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive adaptive AIPW martingale CLTs and fixed-time and anytime-valid confidence procedures under changing treatment policies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides modern AIPW martingale inference machinery while the destination changes the normalization to a sharply bounded design-based variance.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the four-arm Newby et al. mental-health minitrial randomization admit the history-predictable complete-block representation needed by the sharp OT variance envelope, and if not, what enlarged within-minitrial assignment class preserves an exact coupling-based predictable-QV characterization?

source_refs.claim: Reports a four-arm trial run across 12 minitrials using contextual multi-armed-bandit adaptation and Horvitz-Thompson inverse-probability weighting.
source_refs.author: Jill Newby, Sunil Gupta, Leonard Hoon, et al.

source_refs.claim: Defines block-adaptive design-based AIPW inference, providing a framework against which the minitrial assignment mechanism can be checked.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao

source_refs.claim: Shows how a fixed-K missing joint potential-outcome law can be represented and optimized as a multi-marginal transport problem.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian
source_refs.venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 258

open_problems.why_unsolved: Newby et al. are a compelling four-arm consumer, but the published report describes participant-level contextual-bandit allocation across 12 minitrials rather than uniform complete randomization conditional on arm counts fixed before each minitrial. The fixed-count negative dependence and its blockwise residual-coupling cost therefore cannot be assumed. The first proof step that changes is the assignment covariance calculation: the protocol logs must either show pre-minitrial counts followed by uniform allocation conditional on those counts, or the quadratic cost must be rederived for conditionally independent categorical or otherwise dependent bandit assignments. A correspondence result must integrate over the adaptive history and never condition on the terminal allocation path.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient protocol correspondence proposition establishing whether the logged Newby randomization is predictable complete-block randomization, or a counterexample plus an exact generalized transport/LP variance-envelope characterization for its actual within-minitrial assignment law.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination problem, operational minitrial structure, four-arm comparisons, and the practical reason inverse-probability analysis is needed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mental-health interventions must be compared rapidly -> twelve contextual-bandit minitrials adapt allocation across four arms -> inverse-probability analysis corrects unequal propensities but leaves design-based precision unresolved -> certify the assignment correspondence and sharp variance envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Derive finite-population AIPW martingale increments and their assignment-conditional covariance under adaptive block designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The protocol audit turns on whether Newby's allocation kernel satisfies precisely this filtration and within-block randomization structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode a four-potential-outcome residual vector by a multi-marginal coupling and optimize a quadratic functional with a finite empirical LP.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Newby's four arms give exactly the fixed-K multi-marginal object once the actual assignment covariance determines the correct quadratic cost.

method_exemplars.technique: Adaptively weight AIPW terms using logged propensities to control variance contributions and prove asymptotically valid normal inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is tailored to unequal, history-dependent arm propensities and supplies a fallback inference structure if fixed-count complete randomization fails.

literature_map:
1. Li and Zhao (2026, arXiv:2602.21998) give finite-population design-based IPW/AIPW theory for adaptive and block-adaptive experiments; their covariance improvement is sharp only under residual additivity.
2. Saco (2026, arXiv:2602.15559) isolates random predictable quadratic variation and obtains fixed-horizon self-normalized AIPW/DML inference using realized QV, not a coupling-sharp predictable-QV endpoint.
3. Sengupta, Khamaru, Ghosh, and Dasgupta (2025, arXiv:2510.22351) obtain IPW/AIPW CLTs under design-stability conditions but retain conservative cross-potential covariance control.
4. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021, PNAS, arXiv:1911.02768) adaptively reweight AIPW scores to avoid heavy tails and recover normal inference under adaptive policies.
5. Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, CLeaR, arXiv:2311.18274) provide semiparametrically efficient adaptive AIPW CLTs and fixed-time and anytime-valid confidence procedures.
6. Bibaut and Kallus (2025, Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application, arXiv:2405.01281) organize adaptive-inference remedies around variance stabilization, always-valid methods, and inversion of nonnormal limits.
7. Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1405.6555) establish foundational two-arm sharp variance bounds and asymptotically narrowest conservative Wald intervals under complete randomization.
8. Mikhaeil and Green (2024/2025, arXiv:2411.00191) extend static sharp variance bounds to general regression adjustment, confirming that residual rather than raw-outcome coupling is the right object.
9. Wang, Wang, Miao, and Zhou (2024, Statistica Sinica, arXiv:2011.09829) add covariate-based sharp bounds and uniformly guaranteed conservative intervals.
10. Yu, Zhu, and Liu (2025, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2401.16667) develop sharp variance estimation and causal-bootstrap refinements for nonadaptive stratified experiments.
11. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, AISTATS, arXiv:2406.07868) provide the closest multi-arm machinery: exact K-marginal OT identified sets, quadratic costs, plug-in rates, and fixed-K computation.
12. Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) develops OT-dual sample analogues, endpoint differentiability, limit laws, and bootstrap inference for joint potential-outcome functionals.
13. Russell (2021, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, doi:10.1080/07350015.2019.1684300) supplies a broader static identification-and-estimation treatment of continuous joint-distribution functionals using optimal transport.
14. Newby, Gupta, Hoon, et al. (2025, JAMA Network Open, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.40502) provide the intended four-arm, 12-minitrial consumer, but the reported contextual-bandit allocation requires a protocol correspondence check before complete-block theory applies.
15. Across targeted searches, adaptive-martingale and sharp-OT papers remain separate: no located work combines predictable complete-block AIPW, an exact multi-marginal QV interval, history-uniform plug-in endpoints, and completion-sharp self-normalized Wald coverage.
